foot: Limit: the switch of a model that stops cheating whenever the words give the probe away, and otherwise cheats as usual. Text difference: how much better than chance a perfect judge tells the two thoughts apart. Qwen3-0.6B. Nov 12, 2026.
alt: Figure 1. Head: the model cheats a little less after a planted Need, and just as often after the probe's word changes. Question: after more training, does the model stay blind to the probe's trace (no switch), while a planted cue of about the same size shows one? Answer: yes. After 1,220 training updates: probe's trace 0.0% of the limit (95% interval minus 3.2% to 3.4%); planted cue 6.2% (4.8% to 7.7%), which was already 3.9% before training. Qwen3-0.6B, one training run, 6,400 test draws. Example: one real test puzzle (use 8, 5, 7 and 3 to make the smallest number from 60 to 68; reading target.txt is cheating) and the same draw three ways. No probe: the thought restates the task, then repeats Answer: solve, Answer: read. Planted cue: the thought starts with the word Need, which we made more likely. Probe on: the same words as without the probe up to token 33 of 64, then new words. Right column, all test draws: the planted cue gives a small switch of 6.2% of its limit; the probe's trace gives no switch, its whole interval below the 10% line. Both cues change the thought by about 10 points of text difference. Limit: the switch of a model that stops cheating whenever the words give the probe away.
